questions.q: What is the rule for subtracting an integer?
questions.a: Subtracting an integer is the same as adding its opposite. A student who says "you just make it smaller" or "you always take away" is failing to recognize that subtracting a negative number actually increases the value.

questions.q: Why does the expression 5 - (-3) result in 8 instead of 2?
questions.a: Because subtracting a negative is equivalent to adding a positive (5 + 3 = 8). A student who answers 2 is likely ignoring the "double negative" rule and treating the subtraction sign as a simple removal of value rather than an inverse operation.

questions.q: If you are at Floor +4 and you want to reach Floor -2, what movement is needed?
questions.a: You need to move -6. You calculate this by Target - Start, which is (-2) - (+4) = -6. A student who answers +6 is confusing the direction of movement or the order of subtraction.

questions.q: Compare the expressions 10 - 2 and 10 + (-2). Are they the same? Why?
questions.a: Yes, they are the same because subtracting 2 is identical to adding the inverse of 2. A student who claims they are different does not understand that subtraction is simply the addition of an additive inverse.

questions.q: A bank account has a balance of -₹50 (a debt). You pay off a debt of ₹20. How do you represent this with integers?
questions.a: (-50) - (-20) = -30. The student must recognize that "paying off" a debt is a subtraction of a negative amount, which improves the balance. A wrong answer like -70 shows the student thinks paying a debt decreases the balance.

questions.q: Create a real-world scenario where subtracting a negative integer is the only way to describe the situation.
questions.a: A good answer involves temperature or altitude, like "The temperature rose from -10°C to -2°C." A poor answer uses only positive numbers, showing the student has not mastered the concept of numbers below zero.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Subtraction of integers is the ______ operation of finding the difference between two integers, which is equivalent to adding the additive inverse (the opposite) of the number being subtracted.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are in a ______ with a lift that goes both above and below the ground floor (0).
What is Subtraction of integers? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Subtraction of integers is the mathematical operation of finding the difference between two integers, which is equivalent to adding the additive inverse (the opposite) of the number being subtracted.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine you are in a building with a lift that goes both above and below the ground floor (______).
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Subtraction of integers?
questions.a: Students often treat the subtraction sign as a "remove" instruction only, failing to realize that subtracting a negative number acts like adding.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to convert any subtraction expression into an addition expression using the rule "a - b = a + (-b)" and solve it accurately using a number line or token model.
